TechnologyStack.Framework: Go HTTP API, PostgreSQL, MinIO, Redis/asynq, Python workers, React Web UI, Telegram adapter, MCP adapter

ArchitectureShape.goal: Make the API the durable product authority for media accumulation, curation, execution, artifacts, diagnostics, and retention.
ArchitectureShape.canonical-chain: media_item -> collection/inbox -> immutable selection -> analysis_run -> artifacts
ArchitectureShape.control-plane: Go API owns public contracts, owner scope, lifecycle transitions, validation, idempotency, retention policy, diagnostics, artifact metadata, and adapter-visible state.
ArchitectureShape.execution-plane: Python workers consume sealed selection material through internal execution contracts and report progress, artifacts, and diagnostics back to the control plane.
ArchitectureShape.queue-plane: Redis/asynq remains an execution transport only; queued work does not define user-facing product concepts.
ArchitectureShape.object-plane: MinIO stores source bodies, previews, generated artifacts, private execution evidence, and diagnostic bundles behind API-issued access decisions.
ArchitectureShape.adapters: Telegram, Web, and MCP are thin clients over the same API-owned media_item, collection, selection, analysis_run, artifact, and diagnostic state.

component.role: Go HTTP API, WebSocket server, storage orchestrator, and owner-scoped product authority
Python report and research execution behind analysis_run
React management UI for inbox, collections, selections, runs, artifacts, and diagnostics
Thin Telegram capture and management adapter over API-owned state
Thin MCP tool adapter over API-owned state
OpenAPI and schema source for canonical public vocabulary

table.name: media_items
table.purpose: Owner-scoped durable input records independent of execution.
table.fields: id, owner_id, source_id, adapter_origin, kind, display_name, status, size_bytes, mime_type, content_hash, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, retention_policy_id, diagnostics_id
table.rules: New inputs land in the owner inbox by default; invalid inputs remain queryable through diagnostics.

table.name: sources
table.purpose: Normalized input body and origin metadata behind media_item.
table.fields: id, owner_id, origin_type, external_uri, object_key, text_body_ref, checksum, byte_size, metadata_json, created_at, expires_at
table.rules: Adapters do not bypass the API to write source bodies.

table.name: collections
table.purpose: Owner-scoped named groups, including the default inbox.
table.fields: id, owner_id, kind, name, status, version, created_at, updated_at, archived_at, deleted_at
table.rules: Exactly one active inbox exists per owner; other collections are user-managed.

table.name: collection_items
table.purpose: Ordered membership between collections and media_item records.
table.fields: collection_id, media_item_id, owner_id, position, added_by, added_at, removed_at
table.rules: Membership changes are versioned through the parent collection and never mutate media_item content.

table.name: selections
table.purpose: Immutable ordered snapshots prepared for analysis.
table.fields: id, owner_id, status, source_collection_id, item_snapshot_json, option_snapshot_json, diagnostics_id, created_by, created_at, sealed_at
table.rules: selection rows are append-only after sealing except for diagnostic invalidation metadata.

table.name: analysis_runs
table.purpose: User-facing execution records created from selections.
table.fields: id, owner_id, selection_id, run_type, status, idempotency_key, delivery_preference, evidence_gate_state, diagnostics_id, created_at, started_at, completed_at, canceled_at, expires_at
table.rules: Internal execution rows and queue tasks may reference analysis_run_id, but public clients address analysis_run.

table.name: artifacts
table.purpose: Owner-scoped outputs and evidence produced for analysis_run records.
table.fields: id, owner_id, analysis_run_id, kind, status, object_key, content_type, size_bytes, checksum, preview_json, visibility, retention_state, created_at, expires_at, deleted_at
table.rules: Artifact access is always mediated by the API and scoped to owner plus run.

table.name: diagnostics
table.purpose: Structured failure, warning, and operator evidence for ingestion, selection, execution, adapter, retention, and artifact paths.
table.fields: id, owner_id, subject_type, subject_id, severity, code, message, context_json, correlation_id, created_at
table.rules: Rejected records and partial failures are represented as diagnostics, not hidden drops.

table.name: execution_rows
table.purpose: Internal worker claims, queue state, attempts, and read models behind analysis_run.
table.fields: id, analysis_run_id, worker_kind, task_kind, status, attempt_no, lease_owner, claimed_at, heartbeat_at, finalized_at
table.rules: This table family is internal and cannot reintroduce old public product vocabulary.

LifecycleAndRetention.status-source: Lifecycle statuses are defined in docs/requirements.xml and must be mirrored in contracts.
LifecycleAndRetention.retention-rule: Soft-deleted media_item and collection membership are hidden from default reads but retained until policy permits hard deletion.
Selections remain immutable audit snapshots even if source media later expires; execution must record whether source bodies were available at run time.
Artifacts can expire independently from run metadata; diagnostics must explain unavailable artifacts.
Owner export and deletion workflows must include media_item, collection, selection, analysis_run, artifact, source, and diagnostic records.

AdapterContracts.telegram: Telegram captures input, shows inbox or collection state, lets the user manage items, creates selections, starts analysis_run records, and sends artifact previews or downloads returned by the API.
AdapterContracts.web: Web provides the richest management UI for inbox, collections, selections, runs, artifacts, diagnostics, owner-scoped search, and the surviving retention-touching actions: media soft delete plus artifact access refresh.
AdapterContracts.mcp: MCP exposes stable tools over the same API and never maintains its own durable media store.

EvidenceContracts.contract-evidence: Schema tests must fail if old public product route vocabulary returns to OpenAPI or shared JSON schemas.
EvidenceContracts.storage-evidence: Storage tests must cover owner isolation, immutable selection snapshots, lifecycle transitions, retention, diagnostics, and artifact linkage.
EvidenceContracts.api-evidence: API tests must cover ingestion, inbox membership, collection mutation, selection sealing, analysis_run creation, event polling, cancellation, artifact access, and diagnostics queries.
EvidenceContracts.adapter-evidence: Adapter tests must prove Telegram, Web, and MCP operate over the same API-owned state and do not expose grouped submission modes as durable product state.
EvidenceContracts.runtime-evidence: Runtime smoke must prove a real item can be ingested, selected, analyzed, and resolved as artifacts with diagnostics available for failures.
